newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan markets slide on interest rate comments.
newsitem.headline: Japan markets slide on interest rate comments.

text.p: Tokyo share prices sank, Japanese government bonds slid and the dollar dipped on Wednesday after a senior central banker was quoted as saying the Bank of Japan was considering the right timing to tighten credit.

Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group as saying the central bank was considering the right timing to raise its official discount rate, at which it lends to commercial banks, but that the Bank of Japan did not want to make a hasty decision.

The comment, made at a meeting with executives of Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, the Japanese Trade Union Confederation (Rengo), triggered massive selling of Japanese government bond futures and cash bonds, traders said. Rengo on Wednesday urged the central bank to raise the key rate.

The Tokyo stock market's key index, the 225-share Nikkei average, already undermined by worries over the strong yen, closed down 490.85 points at 19,841.98, after earlier falling by more than 500 points.

The dollar also edged down against the yen on the remark, which fanned speculation that the central bank might be willing to raise its rock-bottom interest rates sooner rather than later. The U.S. currency was around 113.45 yen in mid-afternoon trade after earlier hovering near 114 yen.

The Bank of Japan cut the discount rate to a record low 0.5 percent in September 1995 to keep the economy from faltering. But speculation has been growing that it wants to tighten credit in view of the economy's recovery and amid calls for higher rates from some ruling politicians.
